name: VantaAI
summary: VantaAI is a platform for preventing and detecting image-based abuse, combining digital watermarking, reverse-image scanning, deepfake detection, and guided remediation, including automated assistance for legal reporting and takedowns. Built with a team of three (Anita George, Gowri Arun, T P Shivha Shakthiy) for Girlathon 2025, organized by GDSC MACE, Kalkitech, and Kerala Startup Mission.
motivation: A women's-safety platform that treats image-based abuse as a detection-and-response problem rather than just a reporting form.
architecture: Computer-vision and NLP classification pipelines behind a REST API surface: image protection, reverse-image scanning, deepfake detection, and a guided remediation workflow.
outcomes: 2nd place (1st Runner-Up) at Girlathon 2025, an 8-week hackathon.

name: DelAI
summary: DelAI is a GenAI-era delivery-optimization system that models delivery locations as a weighted graph and applies shortest-path algorithms to cut routing time. Built with Lestlin Robins and Muhammed Basil, it won 1st place at TinkHack 2.0, a 24-hour hackathon at Govt. Model Engineering College.
motivation: A 24-hour team build applying graph theory — Anita's strongest DSA focus area — to a real logistics constraint.
architecture: Weighted-graph modeling layer, shortest-path engine, and a routing heuristic optimized against a multi-objective cost function.
outcomes: 1st place at TinkHack 2.0 (sponsored by DBiz.ai, Wizr AI, South Indian Bank); approximately 20% improvement in route efficiency over baseline heuristics.

name: Cupid's Ledger
summary: A BetaLabs project: a gamified Valentine's matchmaking platform spanning authentication, personality quizzes, matchmaking, profiles, and live leaderboards. Handled 1,000+ users in a single day.
motivation: A short-timeline build meant to actually ship and be used at real load, not just demoed.
architecture: React/Vite frontend with a personality-quiz-driven matchmaking flow, live leaderboards, and Framer Motion interaction states, built for a one-day traffic spike.
outcomes: 1,000+ users engaged with the platform within its first day live.

name: CivicAid
tagline: civic-tech venture pitch — Innowave Pitchathon winner
summary: A startup pitch built with the REsolvers team (Adithyan M Nair, Amal Sajeev, Muhammed Basil, Lestlin Robins, Anita George) for the Innowave Pitchathon in Kollam — a pure business-strategy round with no demo and no code. Won 1st place.
motivation: Innowave stripped the hackathon format down to strategy and market logic — the challenge was articulating why the idea matters as a business.
architecture: Business-model and go-to-market plan for a civic-tech concept; Anita's focus was the product experience and framing of the pitch.
outcomes: 1st place at the Innowave Pitchathon, held at Innerspace Coworking, Kollam.

name: fAImer
summary: fAImer is a smart farming assistant that brings ML-based crop disease detection, expense tracking, and market insights to small farmers, as a Progressive Web App with multilingual support and offline-first usage.
motivation: Designed around accessible technology and practical AI — making image classification and farm-management tooling usable in low-connectivity contexts and multiple languages.
architecture: ML image-classification model for crop disease detection, plus expense-tracking and market-insight modules, packaged as a PWA with offline-first sync and multilingual UI.
outcomes: Working prototype with offline-first sync, multilingual UI, and crop-disease classification.

name: LawGorithm
summary: LawGorithm is a scam-detection and risk-analysis system using NLP-based classification and algorithmic risk scoring, exposed via REST APIs for real-time safety alerts.
motivation: Exploring how NLP and rule-based risk scoring can give people a faster signal about what they're reading before they act on it.
architecture: NLP-based scam-classification pipeline with algorithmic risk scoring and a REST API layer for real-time alerts.
outcomes: Working NLP detection and risk-scoring pipeline exposed as a REST API.

name: StudyBee
summary: StudyBee is an AI study assistant that generates structured notes, quizzes, and formula sheets from source material, reporting roughly 40% reduction in prep time in internal use.
motivation: Built to turn unstructured course material into something navigable.
architecture: Content-ingestion and structuring pipeline that produces notes, quizzes, and formula sheets via algorithmic organization of source material.
outcomes: Reported ~40% prep-time reduction in internal use (self-reported, not independently benchmarked).

name: NeuroBridge
tagline: adaptive support platform for neurodivergent individuals
summary: NeuroBridge is an adaptive support platform for people with ASD, ADHD, Dyslexia, and Dyscalculia, with modular tools for routine management, sensory regulation, emotional awareness, social stories, and focused productivity. Built with Sona Jomon, Gowri Arun, and T P Shivha Shakthiy during Kerala Startup Mission's She Builds Tech 2.0, presented at the IEDC Kerala Startup Summit 2026 Demo Day.
motivation: A modular surface so each person only sees the support relevant to them — the design bet was against cognitive overload, not for feature count.
architecture: Modular feature surface (Routine Visualizer, Sensory Regulation, Social Story Builder, Emotional Check-in, Focus Sessions, Visual Timelines) with dynamic feature activation, adaptive onboarding, and role-based access on React/Vite + Flask/Supabase.
outcomes: Presented at Demo Day among 8 student teams at the IEDC Kerala Startup Summit 2026; continuing with Kerala Startup Mission mentorship. Not deployed at scale or medically certified.
note: She Builds Tech 2.0 · Demo Day, IEDC Kerala Startup Summit 2026

name: TrustHeritage
tagline: multi-layer authenticity framework for digitized cultural heritage — presented at CHORDS 2026
summary: TrustHeritage is an explainable, multi-layer authenticity-verification framework for digitized cultural heritage combining DWT watermarking, SHA-256 provenance, image forensics, and OpenCLIP semantic similarity, tested across 130 controlled verification runs. Presented at CHORDS 2026 (ANRF-sponsored, IIIT Kottayam, July 2026).
motivation: Digitized cultural-heritage media can be manipulated or degraded with no reliable way to verify authenticity.
architecture: Multi-layer evidence pipeline: DWT watermarking, SHA-256 provenance hashing, image forensics, and OpenCLIP semantic-similarity scoring.
outcomes: Presented at CHORDS 2026; 130 controlled verification runs across compression, cropping, resizing, rotation, blur, tonal change, and localized manipulation.

name: SAGE-PI
tagline: structure-aware generalizable detection of indirect prompt injection — RV University research
summary: SAGE-PI is a research project on generalizable indirect prompt-injection detection: a multi-channel approach combining DistilBERT semantic representations, source-structural features, and instruction-conflict modeling, built on a 32,475-sample corpus across seven sources.
motivation: LLM security classifiers tend to overfit to their training sources and fail to generalize to unseen sources or novel attack families.
architecture: DistilBERT-based semantic representation + source-structural features + instruction-conflict modeling, evaluated with leave-one-source-out and unseen-attack-family protocols.
outcomes: A reproducible cross-source, cross-attack-family evaluation pipeline with statistical significance testing.

name: Malayalam Sentiment Benchmark
tagline: movie-disjoint benchmark for code-mixed Malayalam sentiment — SRM University–AP research
summary: A 57,393-comment benchmark across 36 Malayalam movies with a movie-disjoint evaluation protocol, comparing TF-IDF+LogReg, MuRIL, XLM-RoBERTa, and IndicBERTv2. Found a 13.3-point macro-F1 gap between conventional and movie-disjoint evaluation. Anita was recognized as Best Intern, SIF-2026.
motivation: Standard random-split evaluation lets sentiment models memorize movie-specific vocabulary instead of learning to generalize.
architecture: Movie-disjoint train/test protocol, judgeability-gated classification, and a cross-view diagnostic for opinion transfer.
outcomes: 13.3-point macro-F1 gap between conventional and movie-disjoint evaluation, demonstrating that standard protocols overstate generalization on this task.
note: manuscript · SRM University–AP · Best Intern, SIF-2026
